national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of External Affairs has said that several issues came up during the discussion between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Addressing media in New Delhi this evening, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that during the meeting, Prime Minister referred to India’s concerns and underlined that both sides should show sensitivity to each other’s core concerns. He added that the concerns should be be guided by the three mutuals which are mutual respect, mutual interest, and mutual sensitivity. In reply to a question on the attack on the commercial vessel MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman, Mr Jaiswal said that targeting commercial shipping, seafarers, civilians, and civilian infrastructure in the region is unacceptable to India. He said, India also urges that free and safe navigation, as well as the flow of commerce through international waterways in the region, be restored at the earliest. He said, the attack on the vessel occurred off the coast of Oman involving a Panama-flagged vessel carrying 14 Indian national seafarers. He said, of them , 13 have been rescued and one Indian national, a seafarer who was on board the vessel, remains missing. Mr Jaiswal informed that search and rescue operations are continuing with the assistance of the Omani authorities, and Indian Embassy is in close contact with them. When asked about the reward of 70 lakh Pakistani rupees announced by Pakistan on Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar, the spokesperson said that such gimmicks and attempts at hoodwinking by Pakistan are not new as India has seen similar gimmicks in the past as well. Mr Jaiswal said that Pakistan must take concrete action rather than making announcements that are of no consequence. Replying to another query, Mr Jaiswal said the energy cooperation between India and Russia is an important pillar of the bilateral partnership. He pointed out that both countries have been collaborating for a long time now on nuclear sector. He added that the Kudankulam project is a successful example of India-Russia collaboration in the energy field. He said India wants to take this energy cooperation with Russia forward. He also informed that both sides have been in conversation, and technical teams have been in discussions. The spokesperson said External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar held a meeting with the Saudi Foreign Minister on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. During the meeting, they discussed regional and international developments. Mr Jaiswal said that the issue of the Houthis was also discussed. There was recently an attack on Saudi Arabia, which India has condemned. He further stated that New Delhi is deeply concerned with the escalation in the situation in the Red Sea region. India has condemned the attacks on Saudi sovereign territory, including on civilian infrastructure and economic assets. Mr Jaiswal said such attacks undermine regional stability and threaten freedom of navigation through the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb. He termed these actions as unacceptable, and hoped for the early restoration of peace and stability in the region. He added that India continues to receive energy supplies from that part of the world.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 30 Finance Ministry clarifies no charges on person-to-person UPI transactions
national_raw_news.content: The Finance Ministry today clarified that there will be no charges at all for person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions irrespective of transaction value. The Ministry said that charges will apply only to person to merchant (P2M) transactions exceeding two thousand rupees. It said that UPI app providers are explicitly prohibited from levying platform fees or hidden charges. The Ministry said that banks have been advised to ensure that merchants do not pass Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) charges to customers for UPI payments. A nominal MDR of 0.4 percent will be levied on Person to Merchant transactions above two thousand rupees while for high-value transactions of 75 thousand rupees and above, MDR will be capped at three hundered rupees per transaction. The Ministry informed that Small merchants receiving up to one lakh per month via UPI QR codes under the Person to Person Merchant (P2PM) classification will continue to enjoy mandatory zero MDR for all transactions. Additionaly, Railways, telecom, insurance, fuel sectors, agriculture inputs will pay a flat MDR of five rupees per transaction above two thousand rupees. It said There are no monthly quotas, volume limits, or tiered caps on free UPI transactions for individuals. The Government has amended the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007 empowering the government to notify specific electronic payment modes where no charges shall apply. It issued a notification under this framework, specifying that Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions up to two thousand rupees will attract zero Merchant Discount Rate (MDR). The new MDR framework will make UPI self-sustainable, give incentives for further expansion in rural and semi urban areas and maintain competitiveness, while ensuring that large majority of payments remain free of charge.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 42 Six states sign agreement for rejuvenation of Yamuna River
national_raw_news.content: Chief Ministers of Six States today signed the Kishau Multipurpose Dam Project agreement for the rejuvenation of the Yamuna River. These States are Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi. The agreement was signed in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Shah expressed confidence that once the project is completed, this event will become an important chapter in history. He said that the Central government has declared the Kishau Project a National Project. Mr Shah said, the Central Government will bear approximately 90 per cent of its financial burden, while the remaining 10 per cent will be borne by the participating states. The Minister said that ever since Rekha Gupta became the Chief Minister of Delhi, continuous work has been underway to clean the Yamuna. He said that since Narendra Modi became Prime Minister, this is the tenth water related dispute, which is now set to be resolved. He said that first, in August 2018, the dispute over the Lakhwar Multipurpose Project was resolved. In the same month, the dispute over the Shahpur Kandi Dam Project was settled. In 2021, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh reached an agreement on the Ken-Betwa Link Project, benefiting the water-stressed region of Bundelkhand. The dispute over the rehabilitation of families displaced by the Narmada Project was resolved in July 2026. Union Minister for Jal Shakti C.R. Patil, Union Home Secretary, Union Secretary for Water Resources, and the Chief Secretaries of the concerned states were also present on this occasion.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 159 Integration of Forces, R&D institutions & Industry can make India self-reliant in defen...
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today emphasisied that self reliance in defence sector can be achieved through seamless collaboration among the Defence Forces, Research and Development institutions and the industry. He called for greater dialogue, co-development and co-production to accelerate technology adoption and strengthen India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem. Addressing the DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet, ‘VIMARSH 2026’ in New Delhi, Mr Singh said that DRDO has demonstrated its capabilities in every field, from missiles to radars, combat aircraft to submarines, electronic warfare system to Artificial Intelligence. The Defence Minister said that the reforms witnessed in the defence sector over the past few years are unprecedented and several game-changing decisions have also been taken. These include the Positive Indigenisation List, the Make in India initiative, iDEX, ADITI and the decision to allocate 25 percent of the Defence Research and Development budget to the private sector. Mr Singh asserted that these measures have been taken to ensure that India does not remain dependent on imports in the defence sector, but moves towards self-reliance. Describing MSMEs as a backbone of the Indian economy, Mr Singh said that their contribution in components, sub-systems and essential services is significant in the defence sector. He added that MSMEs will have to continuously focus on quality, delivery, innovation and global standards, as well as increase partnerships with large companies. The Defence Minister stressed that a new wave of defence startups is rising in India. He said that these startups are not only innovative but also agile and are disrupting the traditional defence manufacturing model. The Minister said that the opportunities in the defence sector have increased for them with funding, mentorship, and market access. Mr Singh underlined that the goal of Viksit Bharat is not merely to build an economically strong nation, but to also make it technologically self-reliant, socially inclusive, environmentally sustainable, and strategically secure. He emphasised that a nation that possesses its own technology holds the power to shape its own future, adding that self-reliance must become an integral part of the country’s character and attitude. During the event, nine licensing agreements for Transfer of Technology were handed over to 13 manufacturing partners to enable commercial production of state-of-the-art systems. DRDO also signed a contract with Quality Council of India for System for Advance Manufacturing Assessment and Rating version 2.0 to benchmark the manufacturing maturity of domestic defence enterprises.

national_raw_news.title: Govt promotes sports as important part of nation-building under ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’ initiative: State Sports Minister Raksha Khadse 5 hours ago 76
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Nikhil Khadse said progress in sports is an important aspect of nation-building as India works towards its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047. The Union Minister, who arrived in Mizoram on a three-day visit visited the Sports Authority of India centre at Mission Veng. There, she met Mizoram Sports Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar, officials of the Sports Department and representatives of various sports organisations, who apprised her of their needs and concerns. Speaking exclusively to Akashvani News, Khadse said the government is making every effort to promote sports as it is an important part of nation-building under the ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’ initiative. She said the government has launched Yuva Connect to enable sports to go hand in hand with education, with various programmes aimed at promoting sports being conducted in educational institutions. The Union Minister said Mizoram is doing well in various sports disciplines and praised the state’s efforts to identify and nurture young talent. She said she would make every effort to promote development across different sports disciplines. Khadse said young people are the vision of the nation and that the government gives them priority. She said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been taking steps to promote sports in India since 2014, with various developments taking place under the Khelo India programme. She said efforts are being made through various initiatives to produce more successful athletes, including identifying talented children in cities as well as remote areas, and that many have already benefited from such programmes. She said women’s sporting talent is also being promoted, but much more remains to be done. Stressing the importance of a systematic approach to sports, she said the government is making every effort to provide athletes with greater strength and support, including through proper nutrition, and to build the infrastructure needed for the overall development of sports.

national_raw_news.title: Workforce participation rate for 15yrs and above increased to 52.8 % in August, highest since March 3 hours ago 49
national_raw_news.content: The Country’s overall workforce participation rate (WPR) for age 15 years and above increased to 52.8 per cent in August, the highest level recorded since March, 2026. According to the monthly labour force and unemployment data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, rural WPR increased by 1.3 per cent to 55.8 per cent, whereas the urban WPR declined half a per cent to stood at 47 per cent in August. The country’s unemployment rate for persons aged 15 years and above declined marginally to five per cent in August, compared with 5.1 per cent in July this year. According to the monthly labour force and unemployment data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, the rural unemployment rate eased to 4.1 per cent in August, which is the lowest level since January this year. In contrast, the urban unemployment rate increased slightly to 6.8 per cent, marking a four-month high. Among females, the overall unemployment rate declined to 5.1 per cent, while the unemployment rate among males eased to 4.9 per cent in August. The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for age 15 years and above increased moderately to 55.6 per cent in August.

national_raw_news.title: Modern biotechnology to be translated into technologies to deal with real agricultural challenges: Dr Jitendra Singh 2 hours ago 47
national_raw_news.content: Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today said that India is witnessing simultaneous advances in plant and human biotechnology as part of BioE3 policy and the biotechnology push under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The Minister today inaugurated SpeedSeed Phenotyping and Resource Optimization for Unified Trait Analysis (SPROUT) facility at BRIC-National Institute of Plant Genome Research in New Delhi. Dr. Singh said that modern biotechnology must increasingly be translated into technologies that can respond to real agricultural challenges and provide tangible benefits to farmers. He said that the scientific advances being made today, particularly in genomics, gene technologies, precision phenotyping and accelerated breeding, will become increasingly relevant in the years ahead. He said that the country’s biotechnology journey is increasingly being driven by the convergence of advanced science, technology and applications that can address challenges relating to agriculture, health, sustainability and national development. The Minister also called for stronger interaction between scientific institutions and industry partners, farmers and other stakeholders. He said, facilities like SPROUT demonstrate how modern biotechnology can contribute to the development of climate-resilient and productive crops, strengthen India’s agricultural capabilities and support the goal of a more self-reliant agriculture sector. SPROUT is a season-independent, controlled-environment facility designed for high-throughput phenotyping, precision stress screening and evaluation of germplasm, breeding populations, mutants, transgenic and genome-edited lines. With a major focus on chickpea, the facility will help connect advances in genomics and genome editing with precise trait evaluation and breeding. This will strengthen the ability to move more efficiently from gene discovery to trait validation and ultimately to crop improvement.
